name: 430. An extra param cannot supply a price-affecting unified field the request did not send (extra-params-price-field)
description: Contract C4, agreement three: a field that affects the price is either delivered or refused with 400 caller_unsupported_parameter naming it. Core checked that for the request's own unified fields only. A price-affecting field named among the extra params (extra_params.size, .n, .dimensions, .speed) was merged into the vendor's body, or read there by the converter, with no unified field showing it, so the vendor billed for a size, a count or a speed the gateway never saw. Only the Tencent provider guarded it, with its own list. schemas.CheckExtraParamPriceFields now refuses, in the request worker before a key is chosen and for every provider, an extra param that names a price-affecting field of the operation's C4 table when the request did not send that field itself. The name is compared ignoring letter case. A field the request did send keeps working, including where the handlers keep it among the extra params for converters that read it there; a vendor's own name for the field (BytePlus ratio) and the three fields C4 exempts (prompt, seed, negative_prompt) are not refused. The rule is pinned in Go over every operation and field of the table and through the real worker (TestCheckExtraParamPriceFieldsRefusesEveryC4FieldOfEveryOperation, TestRequestWorkerRejectsPriceFieldAmongExtraParamsBeforeUpstream). These rows pin it on the /openai drop-in routes, the HTTP routes on which extra_params is unwrapped: embeddings, image generation and speech. The last row is the control: the same field sent as the request's own is delivered. Video create has no row because no HTTP route unwraps extra_params for it; its fields are covered in Go.
